newsitem.title: USA: Clinton help sought in finding missing witness.
newsitem.headline: Clinton help sought in finding missing witness.

text.p: The chairman of the House of Representatives committee investigating alleged campaign finance abuses asked on Monday for President Clinton's help in obtaining evidence from a big Democratic contributor thought to have fled to Thailand.

House Government Reform Committee Chairman Dan Burton, an Indiana Republican, wrote Clinton and Thailand's ambassador to the United States Nitya Pibulsonggram to help obtain testimoney from Pauline Kanchanalak.
Burton said Kanchanalak may have "crucial knowledge" regarding fund-raising activities and the influence of foreign governments on U.S. politics.
Kanchanalak was believed to be in her native Thailand. She donated $235,000 to the Democratic National Committee which was returned by the party because its origin could not be verified.
Earlier this month Burton asked for administration help in seeking testimony of Charles Yah Lin Trie, another large contributor to Democrats who was believed to be in Shanghai.

Burton's panel was conducting a campaign finance investigation separate from the Senate hearings which continue this week. Both chambers are looking into whether illegal campaign contributions were made during the 1996 presidential and congressional elections.
